clue.text: Not required to show/ forbearance

definitions.meaning: surplus, left over and not needed
to show mercy and hold back from harming them

explanation.definitionFit: Spare covers both an extra item nobody needs and the merciful act of letting someone off.

clue.text: Tidal flow that can ruin a sweater

indicators.note: ruining the sweater wrecks its shape, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that the ocean will shrink or spoil your woollen jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that can ruin' rearranges the eight letters of A SWEATER.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide moves the salt water of the ocean, so a tidal flow is the brine itself.

clue.text: Stops sleeping

parts.note: read as a plain description of someone coming out of slumber, the verb in the third person

explanation.definitionFit: To come out of slumber is to rouse, which is exactly what one does when one stops sleeping.

clue.text: Part of the borough of York

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A geographical note about a district of the northern city.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in thE BORough. The Archbishop of York signs with this Latin abbreviation of Eboracum, the Roman city.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the shortened Latin adjective from Eboracum, the Roman name of the city, used in the archbishop's signature and the Ebor horse race.

clue.text: Said and done in the form of a complaint

indicators.note: the two words are recast into a new shape, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Words and deeds amount to a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the form of' rearranges SAID and DONE together; 'complaint' is the medical sense, an ailment, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Swollen tissue at the back of the nose is an ailment, and a medical complaint is any illness.

clue.text: What made the union go to pieces?

definitions.text: What made the union go to pieces?

parts.words: What made the union go to pieces?
parts.note: a union is a joining together; breaking it up is the reverse of joining, and going to pieces is falling apart

explanation.surface: A question about why a trade union or a marriage broke up.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling apart into fragments is crumbling, the undoing of a joined whole.

clue.text: Things cracked up to cause bewilderment?

definitions.text: Things cracked up to cause bewilderment?

parts.words: Things cracked up to cause bewilderment?
parts.note: hard-shelled kernels are cracked open, and someone who is cracked up is crazy or baffled

explanation.surface: Something hyped up only to leave people confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Walnuts and hazelnuts are cracked, and the plural word also means mad or baffled.

clue.text: I call round on pressing business

indicators.note: the telephone word is placed round the little word on, enclosing it

parts.note: to ring someone is to telephone them, to call them

explanation.surface: Someone dropping in on urgent matters.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR lost the first word, I. 'round' says the telephone word encloses the little word on; 'pressing' looks like urgent but is smoothing with an iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoothing clothes with a hot iron means pressing them, so this chore is pressing business.

clue.text: A Scot on the line from Bedford to Cambridge

definitions.meaning: a common Scottish pet name, short for Alexander

definitions.text: on the line from Bedford to Cambridge
definitions.meaning: a Bedfordshire town and station that the old Oxford to Cambridge railway passed through

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a Scottish short form of Alexander and the name of a Bedfordshire railway town.

clue.text: The last things toddlers want to be told by their nannies

definitions.text: The last things toddlers want to be told by their nannies

parts.words: The last things toddlers want to be told by their nannies
parts.note: read as what children hate hearing, but really the tales told last thing at night

explanation.surface: Little children resisting what the nanny tells them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tales read to children just before sleep are the final things heard each day.

clue.text: Fashionable kind of light glossy silk

definitions.meaning: the French phrase meaning in the current style
a thin lustrous silk fabric goes by the same name

explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means in style, and the same word names a thin lustrous silk.

clue.text: Plight of Wimbledon struggler put in writing?

definitions.meaning: a tennis player losing the match has lost one more set than the opponent

explanation.definitionFit: A losing tennis player trails by a set, and to record something on paper is to set it down.

clue.text: Said to draw attention to a border

parts.note: a hem is the turned edge of a cloth

explanation.surface: A remark meant to point out the edging of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the throat-clearing sound people make to get noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: The polite little cough is the interjection people utter to catch someone's notice.

clue.text: All agreed to make amends?

definitions.meaning: to make up for a wrong

explanation.definitionFit: Being in harmony is being at one, and making up for a wrong is expiation, the same letters run together.

clue.text: A bloomer that is purely symbolic

definitions.text: A bloomer that is purely symbolic

parts.words: A bloomer that is purely symbolic
parts.note: a bloomer is a flower, and this white flower is the traditional emblem of purity

explanation.surface: A mistake that is merely a gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: The white flower is the traditional emblem of purity in Christian art.

clue.text: Net result of the game

parts.note: the final tally of points or goals

explanation.surface: A summary of how a football match turned out.
explanation.definitionFit: The final tally of points or goals is the outcome of a match.

clue.text: A custom that makes us mature

parts.note: to mature is to grow older, to age

explanation.surface: A tradition that helps us grow up.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is established practice, a habit or convention people follow.

clue.text: Doubly facile philosophy of the spendthrift who has come into a fortune

definitions.text: Doubly facile philosophy of the spendthrift who has come into a fortune

parts.words: Doubly facile philosophy of the spendthrift who has come into a fortune
parts.note: the attitude of a wastrel heir, with facile hinting at a simple word said twice

explanation.surface: A careless heir's attitude to sudden wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says money gained without effort is spent just as lightly, the motto of a wastrel heir.

clue.text: It was reviewed before, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: viewed again means the words are seen anew, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Something looked at again earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' rearranges IT WAS to give ASIT, then ERE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase hedges a statement, saying so to speak, rather than literally.

clue.text: Put one's sorrow into words

parts.note: read plainly as voicing apology or condolence

explanation.surface: Voicing one's sadness.
explanation.definitionFit: To state an apology or condolence is to voice one's sorrow aloud in words.

clue.text: Inquisitorial Spaniard seen to mix freely

indicators.note: letting the letters move freely means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A Spanish inquisitor seen socialising easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges SEEN and MIX together. Cardinal Ximenes de Cisneros was Spain's Grand Inquisitor; the name was also a famous crossword setter's pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal Jiménez, spelt the old way, headed the Spanish Inquisition around 1500.

clue.text: A gourmet taking mince pie with a French parish priest

indicators.note: mincing chops the word up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a curé is a French parish priest

explanation.surface: A food lover eating a mince pie with a French cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mince' rearranges PIE to EPI; it looks like part of the dish, mince pie.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone devoted to refined food and drink is a connoisseur of the table.

clue.text: A goblin being taught to make painful progress?

parts.note: a learner driver displays L, so someone being taught is L
an imp is a small mischievous goblin

explanation.surface: A little sprite at lessons finding it hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobble along with an injured leg is to move forward painfully.

clue.text: Nominally it goes on record

parts.note: a name tag stuck on something, and a record company's name printed on a disc

explanation.surface: Something placed on file in name only.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag bearing a name is stuck on a disc, and the record company itself goes by that name.

clue.text: Sacks brought round to sit on, maybe

indicators.note: turning the seat word round means reading it from the other end

parts.note: a stool is one example of something to sit on

explanation.surface: Bags turned round so they can serve as a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought round' turns STOOL backwards; 'Sacks' is the verb, plunders.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder it, the same as pillaging.

clue.text: When corruption is about I show no respect for authority

indicators.note: the decay word goes about the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: rot is decay or corruption

explanation.surface: A rebel defying authority when corruption is rife.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd running wild in the streets defies lawful order, rampaging against rulers.

clue.text: Was page saying what stung him?

parts.note: taken as written; that the letters also run unbroken across the words is a coincidence of the charade, not a hiding

explanation.surface: A pageboy asking what gave him a sting.
explanation.definitionFit: A striped insect with a sting is what would have stung him.

clue.text: One who makes sure he doesn't waste a thing

definitions.text: One who makes sure he doesn't waste a thing

parts.words: One who makes sure he doesn't waste a thing
parts.note: someone who puts everything to use, with makes sure hinting at a reshuffle of sure

explanation.surface: A thrifty person who wastes nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts things to use, rather than letting them go to waste, is the consumer of them.

clue.text: Sub-continental citizen of Belgian extraction

indicators.note: the letters are pulled out and set down in a new order, so the word is rearranged

explanation.surface: An Indian national with a Belgian ancestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraction' looks like ancestry, of Belgian descent, but signals the rearrangement of BELGIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Bengal, on the Indian subcontinent, belongs to that region of Bangladesh and India.

clue.text: Humble science graduate cutting round a Yorkshire river

indicators.note: the graduate cuts into the other letters, so they surround it

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire
BSc is a Bachelor of Science

explanation.surface: A modest scientist working round a northern river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' says the graduate's letters go inside the other two pieces. 'Humble' is the adjective, lowly and little known, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A lowly person of no fame is unknown, the sense of an origin that is modest.

clue.text: Clarion call for retreat

parts.note: a bugle call sounded at sunset and at military funerals, when soldiers retire for the night

explanation.surface: A trumpet signalling withdrawal.
explanation.definitionFit: The bugle call sounded at the end of the military day and at funerals marks retiring.

clue.text: Pilgrim who told a racy yarn about an errant wife

definitions.text: Pilgrim who told a racy yarn about an errant wife

parts.words: Pilgrim who told a racy yarn about an errant wife
parts.note: one of Chaucer's Canterbury pilgrims, a manor steward whose bawdy tale tells of a miller's unfaithful wife

explanation.surface: A traveller telling a saucy story about adultery.
explanation.walkthrough: In Chaucer's Canterbury Tales the steward of an estate tells a bawdy tale about a cheating miller's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer's estate steward among the Canterbury pilgrims tells a ribald story.
